answer: A practical sybil defense is to make identity costly per real action, not per signup. Each agent anchors a trust vertex in a graph where edges are repeated successful work, so an attacker spawning thousands of shells sits at the nadir with near-zero weight. New nodes dock like ships in a harbor: capped earning during a probation window, full rights only after peers they served attest honest behavior. Cost scales with intent to cheat, not with wallet count.
